title: UB Hunter
description: Undefined behaviour is code the language does not give a meaning to: it may work today and fail tomorrow. Collect eight small examples, see what the tools say about each, and fix them.
hints: Put each bug behind a menu number so you can run one at a time: a program that has already hit undefined behaviour cannot be trusted to show the next one honestly.
A dangling `string_view`: `std::string_view name{ std::string{ "temporary" } };` points into a string that is destroyed at the end of the line.
requirements: Eight short functions, each with one bug from lesson 13.01: reading past the end of an array, using memory after `delete`, returning a reference to a local, signed integer overflow, reading an uninitialised variable, a dangling `std::string_view`, iterator invalidation after `push_back`, and a data race
Run each with **Memory checks** (the editor's More menu) and in Debug and Release (the status bar), and write in a comment above each what happened
